assembled_text: Look again at the gold crown from Cheonmachong. Today it sits under museum lighting, separated from the place where it was buried. But originally, this was not an object made for a museum. It may have belonged to a burial system of status, ceremony, and identity. And that changes the question from “How beautiful is this?” to “Why did placing something this valuable with the dead make sense?” That second question is where the story becomes human.
